{0}Neither figure is an overclock. The GPU lands on the limit its own driver reports as default, and the CPU limits are set to the number this machine's firmware states for a loaded CPU and GPU together. The clamp is a policy the firmware applies to a supply it does not rate highly enough, not a measurement of what that supply can deliver.

This is an experimental, unconfirmed feature that pins two firmware-managed EC bits open for a moment and fires one WMI command, then measures whether the GPU's power actually moved.
It has not been run on real hardware by anyone who wrote it. During the investigation it is built from, forcing this same mechanism on an undersized power adapter left the GPU in a degraded state - driver calls taking 20+ seconds, unable to render - that did not clear until the machine was rebooted, on hardware with a history of GPU-driver crashes.
This offer only appears when the connected adapter is well above this machine's rated requirement, which is the one safeguard behind it. There is no way to preview the result, and no undo beyond a reboot if something goes wrong.
